results.title: October monetary policy meeting: Why a 25-basis-point rate hike is likely this time
results.content:
Copied

The Reserve Bank of India is widely expected to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points at its October 2026 Monetary Policy Committee meeting, taking the rate from 5.25 percent to 5.50 percent. According to policy experts and economists the probability of a 25-basis-point hike is around 75 percent, while the probability of a status-quo decision is around 23 percent. However, a larger 50-basis-point increase appears highly unlikely. [...] Overall, my base-case scenario is that the RBI raises the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50 percent in October 2026. I assign approximately a 75 percent probability to this outcome, around 23 percent to a hold at 5.25 percent and only about 2 percent to a 50-basis-point increase. [...] The market expectation for the end of 2026 is a repo rate of approximately 5.75 percent. However, the range of possible outcomes is wider than the October decision itself suggests. If inflation and crude oil prices remain elevated, the repo rate could eventually move toward 6 percent or higher. If inflation normalises and oil prices fall, 5.50 percent could become the terminal rate for this cycle, experts say.

# RBI MPC October 2026 meeting: When and where to watch rate decision live

## RBI MPC meet: At its August monetary policy review, the RBI kept the repo rate unchanged at 5.25 per cent and maintained its 'neutral' stance

RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra | Image: Bloomberg

Rimjhim Singh New Delhi [...] Readers can also follow the policy announcement and other developments through Business Standard’s live coverage.

### What to expect from the October MPC meeting?

The RBI’s Monetary Policy Committee is expected to start raising interest rates, with a 25 basis points (bps) increase in the policy repo rate at its October 5-7 meeting, according to a Business Standard poll. Eight of the 10 respondents surveyed expect a rate hike.
